definition: A web tracking technique that creates a unique identifier by instructing a browser to draw hidden text or graphics, then analyzing the subtle variations in how different devices render the image.
metaDescription: Learn about canvas fingerprinting, a sneaky web tracking method that identifies users by analyzing how their browser renders hidden graphics.
simpleExplanation: Canvas fingerprinting works like asking everyone to draw the same picture - even with identical instructions, tiny differences in each person's drawing reveal who they are. Websites use this to secretly identify your device.
whyItMatters: Unlike cookies that you can delete, canvas fingerprints are nearly impossible to avoid and work across different websites. This allows companies to track your browsing habits without your knowledge or consent, even in private browsing mode.
technicalDetail: The technique uses HTML5 Canvas API to render text or shapes with specific fonts, colors, and effects. Variations in graphics drivers, operating systems, hardware, and installed fonts create unique rendering patterns that remain consistent across browser sessions, making them effective for persistent tracking.

examples.explanation: An e-commerce site secretly draws invisible text using your system fonts. The way your computer renders this text creates a unique signature that lets them recognize you on future visits, even if you clear cookies or use incognito mode.

Multiple websites owned by the same advertising company use identical canvas fingerprinting code. They can link your activity across all these sites by matching your unique canvas signature, building a detailed profile of your interests.
A banking website uses canvas fingerprinting as part of their security system to verify that login attempts are coming from your usual device, helping detect potential account takeover attempts.
